dek: Plus 10 more new albums from Fontaines D.C., the Avalanches & more, per Pitchfork.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Pitchfork's weekly *New Music Friday* roundup highlights 11 fresh albums worth your time this week.

slides.label: Starlight to Sound
slides.text: Animal Collective's *Geologist* teamed with artist Kyle Simon to turn telescope light from stars into music on *The Sirens*.

slides.label: Fontaines D.C.
slides.text: Fontaines D.C. dropped *Dopamine Chamber*, featuring a surprise team up with *Rosalía* on the track 'Where Is Gone?'

slides.label: The Avalanches
slides.text: The Avalanches released *No Bad Memories*, a 31 song LP built from old commercial jingles and dead tech, featuring Haruomi Hosono.

slides.label: Sophia Stel
slides.text: Canadian artist Sophia Stel dropped her debut for A24's new label, *The Greatest Album of All Time*, made in her home studio.

slides.label: Heavens to Betsy
slides.text: Pre Sleater Kinney duo Heavens to Betsy returned with *Baby's Gone*, their first album since *1994*, compiling old unreleased tracks.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: From A24's new label to DIY mixtapes, indie artists are building their own lanes outside major label gatekeepers.

question: Starlight-made album: intrigued or skeptical? One word.

caption_instagram:
An artist turned actual starlight into a song, and that's just one of the wild albums dropping this week. Pitchfork's New Music Friday roundup includes Fontaines D.C.'s Dopamine Chamber (with a surprise Rosalía feature), the Avalanches' 31 track jingle inspired No Bad Memories, and Animal Collective member Geologist's telescope built project The Sirens, made with artist Kyle Simon.

Also on deck: Sophia Stel's debut on A24's new record label, and Heavens to Betsy, the pre Sleater Kinney duo, finally releasing their first album since 1994.

Whether it's a major label veteran or an artist running their own label from scratch, this week proves there's more than one way to build a sound and an audience on your own terms.

Starlight-made album: intrigued or skeptical? One word.

That's just one of 11 new albums out this week, including Fontaines D.C.'s Dopamine Chamber (featuring Rosalía), the Avalanches' 31 song No Bad Memories, Sophia Stel's debut for A24's new label, and Heavens to Betsy's first album since 1994. caption_linkedin:
This week's Pitchfork New Music Friday roundup is a reminder that there is no single path to building in the music business anymore. Sophia Stel just released her debut on A24's newly launched record label, a sign that non-traditional companies are entering music distribution. Fontaines D.C. used a high profile Rosalía feature to cross genre lines on Dopamine Chamber. The Avalanches spent years building a 31 track project, No Bad Memories, around forgotten commercial jingles, proving patience and a clear concept still win. Meanwhile Heavens to Betsy, inactive since 1994, found a way to release decades old recordings through Kill Rock Stars, and Animal Collective's Geologist partnered with visual artist Kyle Simon to literally convert starlight into an album on an independent label, Outside Time.

For builders and operators outside the mainstream industry, the throughline is simple: ownership of your concept and your catalog creates options, even decades later.

Starlight-made album: intrigued or skeptical? One word.
